source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

Nearby, a row of registers marked with clinical urgency buzzed with intercom pages and forms filled out with feverish hands. A chart revealed the patient's distress: 'Acute myocardial infarction', their condition highlighted prominently. His name was John, and beside his wristband, a nurse had hastily scrawled: 'Urgent surgery required'. The companion, concerned, asked if the situation had improved since they last checked.

Beside her, a companion stood, his hand resting on the arm of the chair. He complained bitterly about the long wait they had endured. The doctor, arriving in his white coat, moved quickly to join her, glancing over the clipboard in his hand.

The emergency room’s intercom whistled, its voice clear and urgent. A nurse called out the patient’s number, scribbling it down on a form. Beside her, the patient, now calm, looked up at them, his brow furrowed in frustration. His wristband clinked softly against the metal surface, a reminder of their situation.

The register of clinical urgency flickered across the nurse’s eyes—intercom pages flashing rapidly, more forms stacked beside her. She looked back to the patient, whose companion continued to complain loudly. Her heart raced with the weight of what lay ahead.

Behind them, another patient was wheeled past the waiting area, a nurse rushing beside, her face a mixture of concern and urgency. The companion followed, his eyes reflecting the same mix of anger and worry.
